column1: # HOW BIG AN EFFECT COULD THE ZERO ROWS HAVE CAUGHT?
# Simulation with resampling: bootstrap the set's genes, add a uniform shift, refit
#   the permutation test, and find the shift giving 80% rejection over 200 replicates.
#     Apoptosis          +0.10 in deep EN (0.99), upper EN (0.99), cycling RG (0.97)
#     DNA repair         +0.05 upper EN (0.84); +0.10 deep EN (0.99), cycling RG (1.00)
#     Oxidative stress   +0.10 deep EN (0.81), upper EN (0.89); +0.30 cycling RG (1.00)
# WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT LICENSE.
#   The zero rows can rule out a moderate effect: +0.10 is above the median effect
#   size in the battery (0.056) and the panel's own translation cell reaches +0.155.
#   They can NOT rule out a subtle one - the panel's cell-cycle effect is +0.054,
#   below the detection threshold, so an apoptotic shift of that size would have
#   been missed. Oxidative stress in cycling RG is weakest of all (+0.30).
#   State the negative as: no moderate or large death, stress or damage response.
# CORRECTION 2026-08-02: an earlier version of this block reported thresholds of
#   +0.05 and called them 80% power. That simulation never resampled - the observed
#   set mean was held fixed across replicates - so it measured the alpha-crossing
#   point, which is smaller than a power threshold. The numbers above replace it.
